text:
When pollen grains in water are viewed through a microscope, they are seen to be in continuous,
rapid random motion.
What causes a pollen grain to move in this way?
A
convection currents in the water
B
bombardment by a single molecule of water
C
uneven bombardment on different sides by water molecules
D
collision with another pollen grain due to their kinetic energies

options.label: B
options.text: bombardment by a single molecule of water

options.label: C
options.text: uneven bombardment on different sides by water molecules

options.label: D
options.text: collision with another pollen grain due to their kinetic energies
